subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept trusting outbound-staged generated HTML when the staged realpath has a shared-state SQLite provenance row and the already-read bytes match the recorded sha256 and size?
rationale: The code appears fail-closed and tested, but the change deliberately expands a host-local HTML read boundary and adds persistent trust metadata, which needs human security-boundary ownership before merge.

options.title: Accept provenance-gated outbound trust
options.body: Approve this content-bound lifecycle and merge once normal exact-head checks remain green.

options.title: Require retention hardening first
options.body: Ask for TTL-based stale-row deletion or chunked pruning before merge if unbounded marker-table growth is unacceptable.

options.title: Reject the boundary expansion
options.body: Close or redesign toward a different delivery mechanism that never re-trusts staged HTML paths.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance-gated outbound trust
recommendation.body: Approve this content-bound lifecycle and merge once normal exact-head checks remain green.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the trusted generated HTML host-read seam and has the clearest history for accepting or rejecting this boundary extension.
